small_guidance:
- The epilogue is already memory-bound and tiny relative to the conv. Tuning BLOCK_SIZE/num_warps on it will not move fast_p; conv dominates the 17.2 ms runtime.
- If keeping the epilogue, try BLOCK_SIZE=2048 with num_warps=4 and reshape grid to (N*C, ceil(SPATIAL/BLOCK)) to reduce register pressure, but expected gain is <5%.
- Consider folding the sum_tensor bias add directly into conv.bias (since sum_tensor has shape (C,1,1,1), it is mathematically equivalent to a channel bias added after conv) only if the LeakyReLU were not in between — it IS in between, so this is not legal. Keep the epilogue as-is.
large_guidance:
- The torch Conv3d dominates: with baseline 8.95 ms and current 17.2 ms, the conv itself is the bottleneck. Replace nn.Conv3d with a custom Triton im2col-style GEMM kernel: program tiles over (N, OC tile, output D*H*W tile), with implicit im2col gather over (IC, kD, kH, kW) as the GEMM-K loop. Use channels-last-ish layout for the input load to coalesce across IC.
- Fuse the entire epilogue (LeakyReLU → +sum_tensor[c] → clamp[-1,1] → GELU) into the conv kernel's accumulator before the store. sum_tensor is per-OC so it can be loaded once per OC tile. This eliminates a full read+write of the (128,64,14,62,62) tensor.
- Autotune BLOCK_M (OC tile) ∈ {32,64}, BLOCK_N (spatial tile) ∈ {64,128,256}, BLOCK_K ∈ {16,32}, num_warps ∈ {4,8}, num_stages ∈ {2,3}. Output spatial is 14*62*62=53816 per (N,OC), OC=64, IC*kD*kH*kW=8*27=216 — small K means a single K loop with BLOCK_K=32 covers it in 7 iterations.
